Hi Alex & Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great to meet the FintechCo platform and hear about the payments reconciliation use case. Per our call, I wanted to recap the key integration points and next steps around API authentication and key management so your security team has a concrete starting point.

Quick summary of what we covered:
- Use case: server-to-server calls from FintechCo backend to Redwood’s hosted inference endpoints for embeddings + reranking (low-latency, high-throughput).
- Auth options discussed: API keys (short-term), OAuth2 client credentials / JWT, and long-lived service accounts tied to your KMS.
- Key management concerns: rotation cadence, scoped keys per environment, audit logging, and automated rotation via CI/CD secrets pipeline.

Recommended next steps (proposed timeline):
1) Technical follow-up: Dev deep-dive with our infra engineer (Dev) — 45 minutes to review SDK setup and sample auth flows (target next Tue).
2) Security checklist: we’ll send a short doc mapping Redwood controls to your compliance questions (SOC2 scope, key rotation policies).
3) PoC plan: start with API keys scoped to a staging model + service account for production; test rotation automation in your CI (2-3 weeks).

I attached our API auth reference and the mutual action plan with dates and owners.

Ask for you: could you confirm whether FintechCo prefers to use a central service account + KMS-backed keys for all production calls, or if you want per-service API keys with shorter TTLs? Also, please share the names of the engineers who should join the deep-dive.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate schedules once I have the attendee list.

Hi Alex / Priya — looking forward to the deep-dive. A few answers and prep items from the Redwood engineering side:  

1) Supported auth flows (high level):
- API keys: simple header-based keys (x-redwood-api-key). Good for PoC and staging; keys can be scoped per-project/model and limited by rate/quotas.
- OAuth2 / JWT (client credentials): Redwood accepts signed JWTs for server-to-server auth; our token validation enforces iss/aud/exp and supports JWK rotation.
- Service accounts: we support minting short-lived tokens bound to service accounts; these integrate with customer KMS solutions (bring-your-own-KMS) for private deployments.

2) Rotation & automation:
- We provide webhook hooks that can notify your CI when a key is rotated; for production we recommend rotating keys every 30–90 days depending on risk profile.
- For long-running production, use service accounts + short-lived tokens (recommended). We also expose an API to programmatically rotate keys and revoke them immediately.

3) Per-model routing and scoping:
- Yes — you can bind keys/service accounts to route policies (e.g., allow model:open-embed-2 for embeddings only). We can demo attaching ACLs to keys in the deep-dive.

Prep for the deep-dive:
- If you can, share a sanitized sample payload (1–2 requests) and the current CI secrets rotation flow.
- We’ll bring a short demo: SDK quickstart (Python/Node) showing both API-key and JWT flows, sample rotation script, and per-key ACLs.

I attached the Redwood API auth reference (same as Marissa).

Talk soon — I’ll schedule the invite for Tue 8/24 9:30am PT unless you prefer 10am.

Thanks,
